article.headline: How to Fail on Purpose: Inversion Thinking as an AI Prompt
article.lede: The tweet is thin framing for a substantive prompt template. The real subject is a structured AI dialogue that operationalises **inversion thinking** — a decision-making technique that approaches a problem not by asking how to succeed but by cataloguing every credible path to failure, then working backwards. Packaged here as a reusable prompt, the technique asks a language model to play Socratic examiner before turning the analysis around.
article.body:
The prompt works in two stages. First, the model asks questions one at a time about the user's biggest challenge — a deliberate pacing device that forces articulation before diagnosis. Second, it maps all the ways the user could fail at that challenge, then uses those failure modes as negative scaffolding: flip each cause of failure into its positive inverse, and you have a de facto action plan. The appeal is structural. It is easier to enumerate mistakes than to enumerate the right moves from a blank page, and the negatives are often more vivid and specific than abstract advice about success.

Inversion as a mental model has roots in mathematics and was adapted into management and investment thinking long before language models existed. The logic holds that complex systems — careers, projects, relationships — are easier to reason about by asking what destroys them than by asking what builds them. The AI framing here adds interactivity: rather than the user performing the inversion themselves, the model handles the mapping while the user supplies the raw problem detail through the Socratic questions.

The practical limitation is the garbage-in problem. The quality of the failure catalogue depends entirely on how honestly and precisely the user answers those earlier questions. A model working from vague or defensive answers will generate generic failure modes — 'poor communication', 'lack of planning' — that produce equally generic reversals. The technique rewards candour and specificity; it punishes the instinct to present one's situation in the best possible light.

The post belongs to a genre of *prompt engineering* content — sharing prompt templates as productivity tools — that is ubiquitous in the AI-adjacent corner of X. The 'changed my life' register is standard influencer hyperbole and should be read accordingly. What survives the packaging is a legitimate prompt structure that applies an old analytical heuristic to a new conversational medium.

concepts.definition: A reasoning technique that approaches a goal by first asking what would guarantee failure, then treating each failure mode as a signpost pointing toward its opposite. Originally a mathematical heuristic, it was adopted in business and decision-making contexts as a way to surface blind spots that forward-only planning tends to miss.

A method of structured inquiry through sequential questions, named after the ancient Greek philosopher Socrates. In the context of AI prompting, it means the model asks the user questions one at a time rather than all at once, slowing down the interaction to elicit more considered answers before rendering any analysis.

The practice of crafting the text instructions given to a large language model to reliably elicit a specific type of output or behaviour. A well-engineered prompt encodes structure, persona, and constraints so the model follows a predictable analytical path without further hand-holding.
